channel.title: BuildLaw: Blog
channel.description: News and explainers on UK construction law: payment reform, retentions, JCT and NEC updates, building safety, adjudication and mediation, explained.

item.title: Are construction retentions being banned? The late payments bill explained
item.description: The UK government plans to ban cash retentions in construction contracts. What the late payments bill proposes, where it stands and what to do now.

item.title: How to write a valid pay less notice
item.description: What a valid pay less notice must include, when to serve it, common mistakes that make it invalid, and example wording you can adapt for your contract.

item.title: Payment notice vs pay less notice: what’s the difference?
item.description: Payment notices and pay less notices explained side by side: who serves them, deadlines, what they must say and what happens if one is missed under UK law.

item.title: JCT 2024: what changed, and what it means for your next contract
item.description: The main changes in the JCT 2024 Edition explained: Building Safety Act dutyholders, new relevant events, email notices, design liability and what to check.

item.title: Smash-and-grab adjudication explained
item.description: What a smash-and-grab adjudication is, why it works when a payer misses its notices, how true value adjudications respond, and how to avoid being caught out.

item.title: How to claim an extension of time
item.description: How to claim an extension of time under JCT and NEC contracts: notices, evidence, programmes, concurrent delay and how EOT protects you from liquidated damages.

item.title: Liquidated damages in construction contracts
item.description: How liquidated damages for delay work in UK construction contracts, when they can be deducted, the penalty rule, caps and what happens after termination.

item.title: Can a court order you to mediate a building dispute?
item.description: Since October 2024, courts in England and Wales can order parties to engage in ADR such as mediation. What changed after Churchill and what it means.

item.title: What is practical completion?
item.description: What practical completion means in UK construction, what the courts say about defects and snagging, and the consequences for retention, damages and insurance.

item.title: Construction variations: instructing, pricing and getting paid
item.description: How variations work in UK construction contracts: what counts as a variation, written instructions, valuation rules, disputes over extras and practical tips.

item.title: The Arbitration Act 2025: what changes for construction disputes
item.description: The Arbitration Act 2025 amended the 1996 Act from 1 August 2025. Key changes for construction disputes: governing law, summary disposal, arbitrator duties.

item.title: JCT Minor Works vs Intermediate: which should you use?
item.description: JCT Minor Works and Intermediate compared: project size, complexity, design and administration, and when to step up to the Standard Building Contract.

item.title: JCT vs NEC: which construction contract is right for you?
item.description: JCT and NEC4 compared: language, project management, risk, payment, change and disputes, with guidance on which suits your UK construction project.

item.title: Collateral warranties explained
item.description: What collateral warranties are, who needs them, step-in rights, third party rights and what Abbey Healthcare v Augusta means for adjudication.

item.title: URS v BDW: why defects from decades ago can still cost you
item.description: What the Supreme Court decided in URS v BDW [2025] UKSC 21 about developers, the Defective Premises Act and the Building Safety Act’s longer time limits.

item.title: The Construction Industry Scheme (CIS) explained
item.description: How the Construction Industry Scheme works: registration, deduction rates, monthly returns, gross payment status and reverse charge VAT.

item.title: Builder gone bust? What contractor insolvency means for you
item.description: What happens when a contractor, subcontractor or client becomes insolvent in UK construction: termination, unpaid sums, retention and adjudication.

item.title: How long is a builder liable for defects?
item.description: How long UK builders and designers stay liable for defects: rectification periods, 6 and 12 year limits, negligence and the Defective Premises Act.

item.title: The Party Wall Act: a guide for owners and builders
item.description: The Party Wall etc. Act 1996 explained: which works need notice, notice periods, the 14-day rule, surveyors and party wall awards for owners and builders.

item.title: Building Regulations dutyholders explained
item.description: The Building Regulations dutyholder regime since October 2023: client, principal designer and principal contractor duties, and domestic clients.
